## ✨ Highlights

- 🌐 **No more 165 s wait at boot on a network without DHCP**: the kernel's `ip=dhcp` leaves the signed command line, and DHCP becomes janusd's own client. A statically configured node answers in about 3 s instead of 3 minutes, and a DHCP node now renews its lease ([#396](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/396), [DHCP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/network-configuration.md#dhcp)).
- 🔄 **Update a cluster in place, in one action**: each member in turn is drained, updated A/B on its own machine, and put back in service once its stick tables are learnt. No new machine, no address or name to follow. On the cluster's page, through `POST /api/clusters/{id}/upgrade` and with `janusctl cluster upgrade` ([#395](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/395), [Updating a cluster](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#updating-a-cluster)).
- 🛟 **A drained cluster member stays drained across a reboot**: the drain is kept on the node, and the Controller drains a member again if it comes back in service by itself ([#391](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/391)).
- 📈 **keepalived's and BIRD's own counters in the Janus exporter**: VRRP advertisements sent, received and with errors; each BGP protocol's state and route change statistics. No new binary, and each metric is mapped to keepalived-exporter's or bird_exporter's name ([#390](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/390), [#397](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/397)).
- 🖥️ **Proxmox VE machines with the guest agent get its option**, and the machines an earlier Controller created show the settings they lack (the `kvm64` CPU model, the guest agent option), applied on demand with one clean restart ([#392](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/392)).
- 🤖 **Claude Code asks before a critical janusctl command, however it's written**: the plugin's new hook asks the installed janusctl what each command does ([#394](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/394)).

## ⚙️ Node

- **DHCP is janusd's** ([#396](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/396), fixes [#162](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/162)):
  - The UKI's command line has no `ip=dhcp` any more. Before, a node on a network without a DHCP server waited about 165 s in the kernel at every boot, its static configuration included: 180 s to an answer before, 3 s now, measured on the same network.
  - janusd's DHCPv4 client (`insomniacslk/dhcp`) renews the lease from T1, keeps it across a janusd restart, and drops the address when a lease runs out unrenewed (RFC 2131: the kernel's lease was kept forever). It sends no client identifier, like the kernel: DHCP reservations keep giving the same address.
  - Any one physical interface may take DHCP, not only the first with a carrier. With no configuration, every physical interface asks and the first lease wins, as before.
  - `janusctl network status` and the node's page say until when the lease runs.
  - NoCloud `seedfrom` over HTTP(S): init takes a lease first. It also failed on every enforcing node before (an SELinux denial on init's socket) - it works now.
  - The loopback interface, which the kernel's `ip=dhcp` brought up, is brought up by janusd.
- **A drained cluster member stays drained** ([#391](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/391), fixes [#356](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/356)): `ClusterDrain` keeps the drain on STATE, and janusd reads it before keepalived and BIRD can see the member in service. A reboot, an update, a crash or a janusd restart no longer puts it back in service before anyone says so. Undrain and leave remove it. `ClusterInfo.undrained_unix` says when the node was last undrained on its own.
- **VRRP counters** ([#390](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/390), part of [#383](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/383)): `janus_vrrp_instance_adverts_sent_total` and `_received_total`, `_left_master_total`, `_priority_zero_sent_total` and `_received_total`, `_advert_errors_total{error}` - from the keepalived dump janusd already reads. A counter keepalived doesn't keep isn't exported as a 0. Grafana gets two VRRP panels and the example rules a `JanusVRRPAdvertErrors` alert ([VRRP metrics](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/vrrp.md#metrics)). The keepalived-exporter extension itself isn't built: SELinux can't limit it to keepalived's dump signals, and it needs a shell (the reasons on [#383](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/383#issuecomment-6482200164)).
- **BGP counters** ([#397](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/397), part of [#360](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/360)): `janus_bgp_protocol_state`, `janus_bgp_protocol_state_since_timestamp_seconds`, preferred and filtered routes in `janus_bgp_routes`, and `janus_bgp_route_changes_total` - BIRD's route change statistics, from the `show protocols all` janusd already reads. Four BGP panels in Grafana ([BGP metrics](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/bgp.md#metrics)). For exact times janusd appends `timeformat protocol iso long;` to the configuration BIRD reads, unless yours sets one.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Updating a cluster in place** ([#395](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/395), part of [#375](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/375)): **Update** on the cluster's page, or `POST /api/clusters/{id}/upgrade` `{members, version, extensions, haproxy, kernel, new_image, reboot_mode}` (admin).
  - Members are updated one at a time. For each one:
    1. The cluster must be healthy first: the other members in service, peers connected, stick tables in sync.
    2. The member is drained, the balancer told first.
    3. Its node updates itself A/B, with its automatic revert.
    4. The Controller waits for it on the target release on its other slot, then for its stick tables to be learnt.
    5. The member is undrained. With BGP, the next member waits until this one announces its routes again.
  - A VRRP cluster's MASTER goes last. A member already on the target is skipped, so calling again resumes.
  - The first failure stops the update. A member that reverted is back in service on its previous release; one not back within 20 minutes stays drained.
  - A member that is one of the Controller's machines is updated through the machine, so its record and Terraform's plan follow. `PATCH /api/machines/{id}` with a version or image change on a cluster member now runs the same sequence for that member alone.
  - The cluster's card says when its members have an update ([Updating a cluster](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#updating-a-cluster)). Recycling stays for what an in-place update can't do: a new machine, fresh disks, another hypervisor.
- **Proxmox VE** ([#392](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/392), fixes [#373](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/373), part of [#372](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/372)):
  - A machine whose image has `qemu-guest-agent` is created with Proxmox's **QEMU Guest Agent** option (`agent: enabled=1,type=virtio`); adding or removing the extension later sets or clears it, with a stop and start of the machine - the option takes effect only then. Before, the agent's service waited for a port Proxmox never gave it. libvirt machines always had the guest agent's channel.
  - The machines an earlier Controller created are not changed by themselves. Their card shows what they lack - the `kvm64` CPU model, the guest agent option - and **Apply settings** (`POST /api/machines/{id}/apply-settings`, admin) gives it to them with one clean restart. A cluster member must be drained first ([Settings an earlier Controller didn't give](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/hypervisors.md#settings-an-earlier-controller-didnt-give)).
- **Extensions that require another** ([#389](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/389)): an extension's manifest may say it needs another, and a schematic naming it without that one is refused with the same words everywhere - the image factory, the site's builder (which ticks the requirement for you), the Controller's pickers, machines and node updates, and Terraform at plan time. No extension requires another yet.
- **A cluster member drained by the Controller and found in service** - rebooted on a release that kept no drain - is drained again at the next check, and the journal says why ([#391](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/391)).
- **The security update badge names the release with the fixes** ([#388](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/388)): right after a release, a node with extensions read "security update → <the version it runs>" until the image factory had built the new one. The Controller now asks the factory again as soon as it knows of a release, which starts the build, and the badge never points at the running version.

## 💻 janusctl

- **`janusctl cluster upgrade NAME VERSION|URL`** ([#395](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/395)): the same in-place update for the clusters of a fleet without a Controller, from the release's assets or a bundle's URL (`-members`, `-kexec`, `-allow-schematic-change`). It is a critical command: the plugin's hook asks before it.
- **janusctl follows the proxy** ([#394](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/394)): `HTTPS_PROXY` for the Controller too - sign-in, certificate renewal, inventory - as the nodes' gRPC already did. `JANUS_NO_PROXY`, when set, replaces `NO_PROXY` for janusctl alone ([janusctl](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/janusctl.md)).
- `janusctl network bgp status` shows each protocol's since as a full date and time ([#397](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/397)).

## 🤖 Claude Code

- **The plugin's hook** ([#394](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/394), fixes [#370](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/370)): before each Bash command, the installed janusctl reads it the way a shell does - pipes, `sh -c`, full paths, heredocs - and says what each janusctl command in it does. A critical one is asked, even with `Bash(janusctl *)` allowed and in auto mode; one it can't read is asked too; reads may be let through with the plugin's **Allow janusctl's reads** option. With no janusctl, or an older one, the hook decides nothing ([janusctl says what each command does](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/claude-code.md#janusctl-says-what-each-command-does)).
- **Claude Code's sandbox as the boundary on the same account**: the settings that keep your other Janus credentials out of its reach, tested ([Claude Code's sandbox](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/claude-code.md#claude-codes-sandbox)).

## 📖 Docs and site

- **The image factory builds a new release for every schematic in use within minutes** ([#387](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/387)): its builds after a release took a visitor's budget, 5 an hour - the last schematics got their update hours late.
- The lab campaign of [v2026.10.28-2](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.28-2.md) ([#386](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/386)).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **DHCP nodes**: a lease that can't be renewed now ends, and its address goes with it - a DHCP server down longer than the lease time takes the node off that network until it's back. Give nodes static addresses, or leases longer than a DHCP outage. The node keeps its reserved address: no client identifier is sent, as before.
- **The first in-place update of a cluster from an earlier release**: those releases keep no drain across a reboot, so each member comes back in service for a moment after its reboot, and the update drains it again at once until its tables are learnt. From this release on, the drain holds.
- **A drained BGP member that reboots** may announce its routes for up to about a second before janusd closes its gate: BIRD starts with the `haproxy_*` protocols enabled. HAProxy answers meanwhile. VRRP has no such gap.
- **Proxmox VE machines created before v2026.10.28-2** now show the `kvm64` CPU model on their card: nothing restarts by itself. Drain a cluster member, then **Apply settings**, one member at a time.
- **BIRD's since column** in `janusctl network bgp status` and the node's BGP page reads `2026-10-29 01:41:34` instead of `01:41:34.348`: a script parsing it sees two fields.
- **Claude Code**: `claude plugin update janusctl@janus` takes the hook; it needs this release's janusctl on the `PATH`.
- **Terraform**: a plan that changes a `janus_node`'s or `janus_cluster`'s extensions asks the Controller's catalog once.
